data.name: Khizr
data.long_meaning: Khizr, also spelled Khezr or Khidr, is a revered figure in Islamic tradition, known as the 'Green Prophet' or 'Green Man'. He is associated with wisdom, divine knowledge, and eternal youth.
data.spiritual_meaning: In Sufism, Khizr is considered a spiritual guide and patron of travelers. The story of Khizr and Moses in the Quran (18:65-82) highlights the importance of trust and submission to God's will.
data.numerology_meaning: The name Khizr is a 3 Life Path Number, which indicates that the person is creative, self-expressive, and communicative. They are often drawn to the arts, and have a natural ability to inspire and motivate others.

It is also a title used in Islamic history and is associated with other names such as Khair, Khairiyah, Khairi, Khairiyah, and Khairi

data.cultural_impact: Khizr is considered a significant figure in Islamic and Sufi folklore. He is mentioned in several Hadiths and reportedly appeared to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) during one of his journeys. Khizr's story has inspired countless artworks, poetic verses, and shared narratives among Muslims around the world. The figure of Khizr has been immortalized in various Islamic forms of art, from calligraphy to miniatures, further solidifying his place in Muslim cultural heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: Khizr symbolizes knowledge, wisdom, and understanding of God's will. He is believed to possess unique knowledge that surpasses the understanding of prophets and saints and is able to intervene in human lives when necessary. By invoking the blessings of Khizr, Muslims ask for his intercession and seek his guidance, particularly when faced with difficult decisions or challenges. The tales and stories about Khizr remind Muslims of their spiritual journey towards enlightenment and the importance of seeking knowledge and wisdom from diverse sources.
